summary: Eliminated the skeleton-flash on /dashboard by resolving its payload server-side at request time, mirroring the settings/page.tsx + SettingsForm.tsx precedent exactly. Three files: (1) app/app/dashboard/page.tsx is no longer "use client" — it is an async server component that reads the firebaseToken cookie via next/headers cookies(), calls verifyIdToken(token) from src/lib/firebaseAdmin, and on success runs the same five reads GET /api/dashboard performs, with the same per-read .catch() fallbacks: prisma.user.findUnique({ select: { username, beta_waitlist_joined_at } }), getUserFreeClimbRecord(uid).catch(()=>null), getUserClimbReplays(uid).catch(()=>[]), getDuelStats(uid).catch(()=>null), getRecentDuelsForUser(uid).catch(()=>[]) in one Promise.all. The whole cookie-read-through-DB-reads block is inside one try/catch whose catch body is empty but for the comment 'Expired or invalid token — DashboardBody will client-fetch via useAuth.', byte-for-byte the settings pattern; any failure leaves initialData = null, throws nothing, and shows no different UI. It does NOT import or call /api/dashboard, requireAuth, or fetch — it calls the underlying src/db functions directly. (2) New app/app/dashboard/DashboardBody.tsx ("use client") holds the entire former page body, unchanged below the state/effect block: the rendered JSX, DashTab, SkeletonCard, tab band, 'Start a duel' / 'Challenge a friend' links, beta banner ternary, PAID_DUELS_ENABLED_PUBLIC-gated WalletCard, DuelRecordCard/Empty, FreeClimbCard/Empty, ClimbReplaysSection, DuelReplaysSection, CreatorPageBand and the error state are all textually identical to HEAD (verified by diffing HEAD:page.tsx against the new file — the only hunks are the header comment, the export shape, the FetchState seed, the effect split, and the loading-guard condition; every line of markup is untouched). DashboardData is now exported from DashboardBody.tsx and imported as a type by page.tsx. (3) app/app/dashboard/layout.tsx deleted — read it first and confirmed it was purely the metadata workaround (its own comment said so) with a pass-through default export and nothing else; the identical `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` Metadata export now lives on page.tsx, which can export it directly as a server component. Nothing in the repo imported that layout (grepped). Behaviour of the client half: FetchState seeds to { status: 'success', data: initialData } when initialData !== null, else { status: 'loading' }; the client fetchDashboard() effect now early-returns on `initialData !== null` (mirroring SettingsForm's `if (!token || initialData !== null) return;`), making the client fetch the fallback path only; the auth-redirect effect was split out and kept as-is (still gates on authLoading, still pushes /auth/signin?redirect=%2Fdashboard when !user || !token) because the firebaseToken cookie and the Firebase client SDK session can disagree in either direction; the authLoading spinner and the `if (!user) return null` guard are now both nested under `if (initialData === null)` so server-populated renders paint content on the first frame — the same restructure SettingsForm uses (`if (initialData === null && (loading || !user))`). SkeletonCard is retained and still renders for the genuine loading state on the fallback path. Checked that both components reachable with a null token during SSR/pre-auth are safe: WalletCard already takes `token: string | null` and early-returns in its refresh callback, and BetaBanner is still behind the existing `token &&` guard. duelStats is narrowed server-side to the four counters DuelRecordCard actually reads (wins, losses, current_streak, best_streak) rather than passing the raw Prisma DuelStats row, so no user_id and no updated_at Date crosses the RSC boundary; every other field (ClimbReplaySummary.createdAt, RecentDuelItem.completedAt) is already an ISO string from the db layer, so the server-rendered payload is structurally identical to the JSON the fallback fetch produces. On force-dynamic: did NOT add `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`, because the settings precedent does not have it and cookies() is itself a dynamic API. Verified rather than reasoned, by the same detached-worktree route-table method the prior two cycles used: `git worktree add <scratch> HEAD --detach`, symlinked app/node_modules, ran pnpm build in both trees and diffed all 125 route-table entries. Baseline HEAD shows `○ /dashboard` (statically prerendered — i.e. the skeleton shell was literally baked into build-time HTML, which is the flash); the modified tree shows `ƒ /dashboard`. Exactly one line moved, nothing else changed; prerender-manifest.json agrees (/dashboard is the only route removed from the static list, zero added). /settings is `ƒ` in both builds with no force-dynamic export, confirming cookies() alone opts the route out — same as headers() did for /duel. All six context/gates.json gates green. Did not touch /api/dashboard/route.ts, requireAuth.ts, firebaseAdmin.ts, or authCookie.ts. No new dependencies. app/next-env.d.ts churn from the builds was reverted and typecheck re-run clean afterwards. Working tree left uncommitted for the verifier.
goal: Eliminate the /dashboard skeleton-flash by resolving the dashboard payload server-side at request time, mirroring the existing settings/page.tsx + SettingsForm.tsx precedent, preserving all existing UI and behaviour.

learnings.insight: The route-table diff showed /dashboard was `○` (statically prerendered) at HEAD, not merely client-rendered. A fully "use client" page with no dynamic API still gets its SSR shell baked into build-time HTML, so the very first bytes every user received were the two animate-pulse SkeletonCards from a shared static file — the flash was structural, not a network-latency artifact. After the change it is `ƒ`. This also means the prior behaviour could never have been fixed by making the client fetch faster.
learnings.action: When diagnosing a first-paint flash on a "use client" page, check the `next build` route table for `○` before assuming the cause is fetch latency. A static `○` on an authenticated page is the tell. Verify the fix flipped it to `ƒ` and that no other route moved, via a detached-worktree baseline build plus a prerender-manifest.json route-set diff.

learnings.insight: Unlike the /duel and /tournaments geo work, `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` was deliberately NOT added to /dashboard. The settings precedent omits it and /settings is `ƒ` in the build table with no such export, because cookies() is a dynamic API exactly as headers() is. The asymmetry is intentional and documented in the page's header comment: on /duel, dropping the headers() call would silently bake a region decision into cached HTML (a compliance failure that still looks like a valid page); on /dashboard, dropping the cookie read simply yields initialData = null and the client fallback takes over, which is a visible UX regression, not a silent wrong answer. Do not file its absence as a defect without first re-checking the route table.
learnings.action: Treat `ƒ /dashboard` in the build route table as the acceptance evidence for rendering mode, not the presence or absence of a `dynamic` export. If a future change drops the cookies() call, the route-table check — not the source — is what catches it.

learnings.insight: With initialData non-null, DashboardBody now renders full content while useAuth() is still `loading` and `token` is null (the authLoading spinner and the `if (!user) return null` guard are both nested under `initialData === null`). That is the whole point of the change and mirrors SettingsForm, but it means two children can now mount with a null token where previously they could not: WalletCard (prop type is already `string | null`, its refresh early-returns on !token, so it paints 0 chips then refreshes when the token arrives) and BetaBanner (still unreachable — the existing `token && <BetaBanner token={token} />` guard holds). A test asserting 'no dashboard content renders while authLoading' would now fail and would be asserting the pre-fix defect.
learnings.action: When testing the server-populated path, assert that real content (DuelRecordCard / FreeClimbCard) is present on first render with authLoading true, and that no SkeletonCard renders. Reserve the skeleton/spinner assertions for the initialData === null fallback path.

learnings.insight: Sixth consecutive cycle: `pnpm build` in app/ rewrites the tracked app/next-env.d.ts from dev type paths to prod ones. Additionally, deleting a route segment file (app/dashboard/layout.tsx) leaves stale generated types in .next/types that make `pnpm typecheck` fail with TS2307 'Cannot find module ../../app/dashboard/layout.js' until a rebuild regenerates them — a red typecheck that is pure stale-artifact noise, not a real error.
learnings.action: After any pnpm build in app/, run `git status --short` and `git checkout -- app/next-env.d.ts`, then re-run pnpm typecheck. If typecheck fails with TS2307 on a route file you deleted, run pnpm build once to regenerate .next/types before believing the failure.
